item.title: The Imposter Inside
item.description:
The Illusion of Being a Fraud

Feeling like a fraud is, above all, a matter of perception. It is about how you imagine others interpret your abilities, your intentions, and your worth. You begin to believe that every action is being observed, every word evaluated, every decision quietly measured against some invisible standard. You assume that people are searching for flaws, waiting for the moment you make a mistake. That mistake becomes terrifying because, in your mind, it does more than reveal an error. It reveals you. It confirms the suspicion you have carried all along—that you never truly belonged, that your achievements were accidental, and that sooner or later everyone will discover the truth. You fear that once the illusion is broken, everything you have built will come crashing down.
